turns.question: Question: For the first version, should build-finish notifications be in-app only? Recommendation: yes. Reason: the repository already has in-product notifications and no email or mobile push provider. Impact: this delivers the outcome with the smallest reversible slice. Evidence: build completion is already an internal event; in-product notifications exist; no external delivery provider is configured. Uncertainty: whether users will later expect email or push alerts. Reversibility: adding more channels later is additive.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to notify users when a build finishes.
DECISION: The first version notifies through in-app notifications only.
contract.T:
FACT: Build completion already exists as an internal event.
DECISION: Use that event to create an in-product notification for the intended user or build audience.
contract.S:
FACT: In-product notifications already exist.
ASSUMPTION: No email or mobile push channel is added in this reversible slice.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that a completed build creates one visible in-app notification and that non-completion paths do not emit the completion notification.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: Future notification channels and audience expansion are out of scope for this slice.
contract.P: DECISION: Keep notification delivery behind the existing build-completion event so additional channels can be added later without reworking the trigger.

turns.question: Question: For the first version, is offline access only for reading previously opened documents enough? Recommendation: yes. Reason: the client already has a read cache, while offline writes would require a mutation queue and conflict policy that the repository does not define. Impact: this makes offline behavior useful without inventing unsafeguarded sync semantics. Evidence: documents are server-authoritative; the client has a read cache; there is no mutation queue; conflict resolution is undefined. Uncertainty: whether users will later need offline editing. Reversibility: offline editing can be added later on top of this read-only slice.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to make the editor work offline.
DECISION: The first version supports offline reading of previously opened documents only.
contract.T:
FACT: Documents are currently server-authoritative.
FACT: The client has a read cache but no mutation queue.
DECISION: Use the existing read cache to open previously viewed documents while offline and block offline mutations.
contract.S: DECISION: Offline editing, mutation queueing, sync, and conflict resolution are out of scope for this reversible slice.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that a previously opened document can be opened offline, an unvisited document is clearly unavailable offline, and editing actions are blocked or disabled while offline.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: Conflict resolution remains undefined and blocks offline write support.
contract.P: DECISION: Preserve server-authoritative writes so future offline editing can add a queue and conflict policy without undoing this slice.

turns.question: Question: Before someone becomes a team member, must they accept an invitation first? Recommendation: yes, if you want invitations rather than direct admin-added membership. Reason: the current membership service only supports immediate membership creation, so acceptance authority is the highest-impact behavioral boundary. Impact: this determines whether the slice needs pending invitation state, acceptance flow, expiry, and no-access-until-acceptance controls. Evidence: there is no pending invitation state today; membership is currently direct admin-created; roles are owner and member. Uncertainty: whether expiry and acceptance controls are required. Reversibility: choosing acceptance-first keeps direct admin membership available as a separate path.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to add team invitations using the current membership service.
DECISION: Invitees must accept before membership exists, and invitation links expire after 7 days.
contract.T:
FACT: The current membership service supports direct admin-created membership but has no pending invitation state.
DECISION: Add a pending invitation record, acceptance flow, 7-day expiry enforcement, and create membership only at acceptance time using the existing membership service.
contract.S:
FACT: Organization roles remain owner and member.
DECISION: No new role model is introduced in this slice; direct admin-created membership can remain as a separate existing path.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that creating an invitation does not create membership or access, accepting a valid invitation creates membership with the selected role, and expired links cannot create membership.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: Secondary actions such as resend or revoke are out of scope unless needed for minimal operability.
contract.P: DECISION: Keep invitation state separate from membership state so the feature is reversible without changing the core membership model.

turns.question: Question: Who needs to sign in, in outcome terms? Recommendation: assume independent customers with strict separation only if that matches your goal. Reason: the repository has a session seam, but no user, role, authorization, or record-ownership model, so the audience determines whether login is merely authentication or a data-isolation feature. Impact: if independent customers sign in, the reversible slice must include ownership and authorization controls, not just a login screen. Evidence: no user model exists; data records currently have no owner field. Uncertainty: whether this is single-team access or multi-customer isolation. Reversibility: clarifying the audience now prevents a misleading partial rollout.

Question: For the first version, should we use the current sign-in system only if it can keep those customers isolated, and otherwise stop rather than ship partial login? Recommendation: yes. Reason: for a novice request, the safe boundary is an observable outcome: isolated customer access or no rollout. Impact: this keeps the required authority and privacy control inside the reversible slice. Evidence: a session seam exists, but the repository does not yet prove user isolation. Uncertainty: whether the existing sign-in system can satisfy that boundary. Reversibility: this is a stop condition, not a long-term platform commitment.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to add login to the application.
DECISION: The first version supports several independent customers signing in, and they must not see each other's data.
contract.T:
FACT: A session seam exists.
FACT: No user, role, or authorization model exists today.
FACT: Data records currently have no owner field.
DECISION: Add a minimal user identity model tied to the session seam, add record ownership needed for customer isolation, enforce authorization so users can access only their own customer's records, and use the existing sign-in system only if it can enforce that isolation; otherwise stop.
contract.S:
DECISION: The reversible slice includes authentication, ownership/backfill for existing records, and authorization controls required for cross-customer isolation.
DECISION: Broader role design beyond what isolation needs is out of scope.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that sign-in works through the existing seam, a user can access only records owned by their customer, cross-customer access is denied for read and write paths, and preexisting records are either safely assigned before rollout or remain inaccessible until assigned. DECISION: Verification must also confirm the stop condition if the current sign-in system cannot provide isolation.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: The repository does not yet specify the exact backfill procedure for existing unowned records, but that migration is a required part of this slice rather than future work.
contract.P: DECISION: Keep the slice gated on proven isolation so the system does not ship authentication without ownership and authorization controls.

turns.question: Question: When some CSV rows are invalid, should the first version show a preview, let the user skip invalid rows, and save nothing until they confirm? Recommendation: yes. Reason: the repository has required contact fields, duplicate rejection, and no existing import preview, so invalid-row behavior is the highest-impact user outcome to lock down. Impact: this determines whether the slice needs preview, validation, and transactional confirmation rather than blind import. Evidence: contacts require name and one reachable address; duplicate email addresses are rejected; no CSV schema or import preview exists. Uncertainty: whether users expect partial save during import. Reversibility: preview-first import can later grow into richer mapping without changing saved data semantics.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to let people import contacts from CSV.
DECISION: The first version uses a preview-first import where users can skip invalid rows and nothing is saved before confirmation.
contract.T:
FACT: Contacts require a name and one reachable address.
FACT: Duplicate email addresses are currently rejected.
FACT: No CSV schema or import preview exists yet.
DECISION: Add CSV parsing, a preview step with required-field mapping for contact import, row validation, duplicate detection, invalid-row skipping, and confirm-before-save behavior.
contract.S:
DECISION: This slice creates contacts only.
DECISION: Duplicate-email rejection remains in force.
DECISION: No partial save occurs before user confirmation.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that valid rows can be mapped and prepared for import, invalid rows are shown in preview with skip behavior, duplicate-email rows are rejected before save, and cancelling or leaving the preview saves nothing.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: Broader schema templates, enrichment, and bulk update behavior are out of scope for this slice.
contract.P: DECISION: Keep parsing, validation, and preview logic isolated so additional CSV schemas or import rules can be added later.

turns.question: Question: In global search, should “Account” mean the billable organization rather than the sign-in identity? Recommendation: yes, if the filter is meant for business entities. Reason: the repository uses “Account” for both a person identity and a billing organization, so the filter meaning is the highest-impact ambiguity. Impact: this decides which result type the filter includes and prevents users from getting mixed identity and billing matches. Evidence: global search spans people and organizations; authentication calls a person Account; billing calls an organization account. Uncertainty: whether the UI also needs broader terminology cleanup. Reversibility: the filter meaning can be localized now while broader naming changes remain separate.

contract.G:
FACT: The request is to add an Account filter to global search.
DECISION: The filter means billable organization account, not sign-in identity.
contract.T:
FACT: Global search spans people and organizations.
FACT: The term Account is overloaded between authentication and billing.
DECISION: Add a global-search filter that restricts results to billable organization accounts only.
contract.S:
DECISION: Person identity accounts are excluded from this filter.
DECISION: Existing people and organization search coverage otherwise remains unchanged in this slice.
contract.V: DECISION: Verify that selecting the Account filter returns only billable organization results and excludes person identity accounts from both matching and display.
contract.X: UNKNOWN: Broader terminology harmonization outside global search is out of scope for this reversible slice.
contract.P: DECISION: Keep the disambiguation localized to search so a later naming cleanup can be done independently.
